title: One item of the evidence of a registry entry
description: What backs a name, a type or a sentence, in our own words. The entry the item concerns is named by its registry id (`concerns`); in the sentence a function the registry names is cited as code:<id>, and a place with no id of its own is an address with its binary and build (registry/README.md, "Citing code and tests"); a test by its path under tests/ without the extension, its case and step as deeper levels. What the kinds carry is the bar of registry/README.md, "Rungs": a read and a watch together or a test confirm a name of ours, game-name and toolkit-name put a thing on the store's rung, and reach, pairing, extender-name and text lift nothing.

kind.description: A memory watch caught the code writing or reading what the entry says.
A value read in a running game agrees with the entry.
The entry was paired with a function or type of another build or of the Toolkit.
The game's own name: the macOS build's symbols, FieldMeta, a type name the engine keeps as text.
A counter showed the code running in a situation (a coverage pass, a count of calls): that it ran and when, not what it does.
Script Extender's own name or declaration.
A test in the game proves it.

test.description: The test's path under tests/ without the extension, then its case and its step: combat/attack/ranged/crossbow/aim.

kind.description: A sentence carried over from an earlier store, not yet split into items of the kinds above.

store.description: Written by the tool that looked the name up, never by hand: the store that holds it - a Toolkit binary (EoCShared.dll), the macOS build (bg3_macos_x64), the type names the executable keeps (type-names).

tie.description: With `store`: what ties the store's name to this thing. match - the symbol database matched the Toolkit's export to this function; pair - a stored pair (a seed or an accepted pair of `decomp pair`) joins the macOS function to this one; name - nothing but the name given.
